label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: As of Aug 8: 93+ Falcon-family launches in 2026 — SpaceX passed its 90th Falcon 9 launch of the year on Aug 4 (Starlink, Vandenberg SFB) and its 50th launch from the West Coast in 2026 on Aug 8 (Starlink, Vandenberg SFB). President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year. Previously: 600th flight-proven-booster launch, Starlink 10-45 (July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1080 28th flight, 638th booster recovery overall); record 36th single-booster reflight, Starlink 10-42 (July 9, B1067, SLC-40). Also in this window: Starship IFT-13 flew (test flight, not counted toward this Falcon-family total) — T-0 abort July 16, successful launch July 24.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 647th: booster landing during the Aug 8 Starlink West Coast mission (163rd touchdown on droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas). 638th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-45, July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — B1080 28th flight; SpaceX's 600th flight-proven-booster launch overall; ASOG's 161st touchdown). 635th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-42, July 9, SLC-40 — B1067's record 36th flight; ASOG's 160th touchdown). 622nd: OCISLY landing (Starlink + Starshield, June 7, Vandenberg SLC-4E). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: 10,898 satellites in orbit (10,882 operational) as of early Aug 2026, out of 12,644 ever launched (per KeepTrack X-Report). SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. S-1 confirmed 10.3M subscribers (doubled YoY); ARPU $66/month (Q1 2026). Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink drove the majority of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue.

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in S-1 filing (doubled YoY). Starlink segment profit: $1.2B in most recent quarter. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 36th flight on the Starlink 10-42 mission (July 9, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights. Previously: 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) is in static-fire testing at Starbase; Musk has floated a late-August window (FAA-dependent), targeting the first delivery of operational V3 Starlinks to full orbit and a possible first tower catch attempt of the upper stage. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq
contestNote: Trading at $133.11/share as of Aug 10, 2026 (~$1.79T market cap; 52-week range $104.83–$225.64). A volatile three-week stretch: SPCX fell below its $135 IPO price for the first time July 15; Aug 4 Q2 earnings (first as a public company) beat on revenue ($7.81B, +92% YoY) but the stock fell ~8% after-hours and then as much as 13% intraday Aug 5 on AI/Colossus capex concerns; the Aug 6 post-IPO lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B, more than doubling public float to 11.8%) yet the stock rose 6.1% rather than falling; shares then jumped a further 15.8% Aug 8 as lock-up fears faded and the pending $60B Cursor (Anysphere) acquisition neared close. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42% economic equity, ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
